ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Confirming eradication

A patient’s dyspepsia improves after H. pylori treatment. He asks whether the disappearance of symptoms proves cure. Which follow-up plan best distinguishes clinical improvement from documented eradication of the organism after treatment?

  1. Use symptom resolution as the only proof
  2. Repeat serum antibody testing immediately
  3. Perform a stool test during antibiotic therapy
  4. Never test after the first treatment course
  5. Arrange an appropriately timed urea breath or stool antigen test
Answer and explanation

Arrange an appropriately timed urea breath or stool antigen test

Symptom improvement does not establish eradication; a test of cure is required.

Option explanations

Arrange an appropriately timed urea breath or stool antigen test: Symptom improvement does not establish eradication; a test of cure is required.

Use symptom resolution as the only proof: Symptoms can improve despite persistent infection.

Repeat serum antibody testing immediately: Antibodies can remain positive after eradication.

Perform a stool test during antibiotic therapy: Antibiotics can suppress the organism and cause a false negative.

Never test after the first treatment course: Confirmation is recommended after treatment.
